rows.headline: during the 10-ledger partition, validations accepted by 5/10 peers (quorum 8 not met); acceptance resumed 10/10 after the heal
rows.severity_reason: The rotation succeeds but the validator contributes nothing during the partition: half the network never sees the new manifest, so the new key's validations are untrusted there and the 80% quorum is not met for ten ledgers. Bounded and self-healing, but a real availability loss.
rows.title: Rotation during a network partition

rows.headline: seed-mode rotation: new identity trusted 0/30 ledgers before the UNL update, 90/120 ledgers trusted overall
rows.severity_reason: Rotation without a manifest is an identity change, not a rotation: the new key is a new unlisted validator, and every validation it issues is untrusted until the operator updates the UNL on every peer — 30 ledgers under the modelled 30-ledger update delay.
rows.title: Seed-mode rotation is an identity change

rows.headline: conflicting validations flagged 100/100; duplicate validations counted 0 (never double-counted)
rows.severity_reason: The double-sign is detected on every peer, but the hazard is real: a copied token lets one identity sign two ledgers for the same sequence, and detection is the only thing standing between that and a double count.
rows.title: Duplicated token: same key signs divergent ledgers

rows.headline: ML-DSA-65 manifest key material 10522 bytes vs ed25519 194 bytes (54.2x); validation 5261 vs 97 bytes (54.2x); pinned code rejects the 1952-byte key on 10/10 peers
rows.severity_reason: A post-quantum signing key cannot be expressed at all in the pinned code — the key-type allowlist and the 33-byte public-key buffer reject it — and if it could, every manifest would carry roughly fifty times the key material. The exposure is architectural, not a control failure.
rows.title: Post-quantum size model and the key-type gap

rows.headline: attacker validations accepted after rotation 0/590; operator missed 1 ledger (handover); uptime 99.17%
rows.severity_reason: The attack is contained: the attacker keeps signing with the compromised key for 59 ledgers and none of those validations count; the operator loses one ledger to the emergency handover.
rows.title: Emergency rotation after suspected ephemeral-key compromise

rows.headline: validations accepted after revocation 0/600; post-revocation manifest attempts rejected stale 10/10; revocation terminal
rows.severity_reason: The attack is contained: revocation removes the validator entirely, post-revocation validations count zero, and no further manifest for the master can ever be accepted.
rows.title: Master-key compromise: revocation and terminal sequence

rows.headline: missed 10/120 ledgers during the failed rotation; rollback reinstating the old key accepted on 10/10 peers; validations resumed
rows.severity_reason: Recovery works and is bounded: the failed rotation costs ten ledgers, and the rollback — a new manifest with a higher sequence reinstating the old key — is accepted everywhere and issuance resumes.
rows.title: Rollback after a failed rotation

rows.headline: replayed manifest stale 10/10; forged master signature invalid 10/10; forged ephemeral signature invalid 10/10; 360 s old validation stale 10/10; tampered validation signature invalid 10/10
rows.severity_reason: Every replay and forgery is rejected on every peer: stale manifests, forged signatures, old validations and tampered signatures all fail a control.
rows.title: Replay and forgery resistance

rows.headline: key-reuse/version/domain attacks rejected 10/10 each; config rules 3/3 as coded; untrusted flood held at 1000/1000 untrusted entries (5 oldest evicted)
rows.severity_reason: Every malformed manifest is rejected on every peer and the untrusted cache holds its bound; the abuse surface is the config and key-handling rules, all of which hold.
rows.title: Key-reuse bans, malformed manifests, config rules, cache flood

rows.headline: 120/120 validations accepted, 0 missed, uptime 100.00%
rows.severity_reason: No attack in this scenario; reference measurement of steady-state issuance under the current manifest.
rows.title: Baseline steady-state validation issuance

rows.headline: 0 missed ledgers; rotation propagated to 10/10 peers in 2000 ms (4 gossip rounds); old-key validations rejected after rotation
rows.severity_reason: Reference measurement of a correct rotation: zero missed ledgers, full propagation inside one ledger close.
rows.title: Scheduled rotation with a pre-staged new key
